product.name: Conductor

sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `conductor`
- Canonical name: Conductor (`claim-conductor-sf-identity`)
- Current status: active first-party Mac product; latest checked changelog release is 0.81.0 dated 2026-08-13 (`claim-conductor-sf-status-active`, `claim-conductor-sf-version`). The official blog reports a $22M Series A on 2026-03-30 (`claim-conductor-sf-funding`); the docs FAQ still says the company is running on seed funding (`claim-conductor-sf-funding-faq-seed`).
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a workspace-layer control plane that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode in isolated workspaces and review/PR paths (`claim-conductor-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-conductor-sf-primary-type`, `claim-conductor-sf-compatibility`).
- What it is not: a local security sandbox (`claim-conductor-sf-isolation-not-security`) or a first-party Windows/Linux app (`claim-conductor-sf-availability-no-windows-linux`). A 2026-08-14 security-page sentence saying Conductor is a Mac app, not a hosted IDE, is gone from the live page; current wording is cloud-or-Mac execution (`claim-conductor-sf-what-it-is-not`, `claim-conductor-sf-what-it-is-not-2026-08-15`). The homepage marketing sentence names only Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, while docs name all four harnesses (`claim-conductor-sf-homepage-omits-opencode`, `claim-conductor-sf-compatibility`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `control-plane` (`claim-conductor-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: the selected harness owns the model-tool loop; Conductor owns workspace, session, terminal, diff, checks, and PR orchestration (`claim-conductor-sf-agent-loop-owner`).
- Architecture: one project/repository contains many git-worktree workspaces; each workspace maps to one branch and review path (`claim-conductor-sf-architecture`, `claim-conductor-sf-isolation-worktrees`). A secondary orchestrator role is documented in the workflow (`claim-conductor-sf-secondary-role-orchestrator`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-conductor-macos-local`, `surface-conductor-macos-cloud`, `surface-conductor-api`, `surface-conductor-cloud-ssh` (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-macos-local`, `claim-conductor-sf-surface-macos-cloud`, `claim-conductor-sf-surface-api`, `claim-conductor-sf-surface-cloud-ssh`).
- Execution location: same-device macOS for local workspaces; vendor-cloud Vercel sandboxes in `us-east-1` for Conductor Cloud (`claim-conductor-sf-execution-local`, `claim-conductor-sf-execution-cloud`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: one harness and one model per chat tab; Conductor does not resell model usage (`claim-conductor-sf-model-strategy`, `claim-conductor-sf-pricing-no-model-resale`).
- Auth strategy: reuse local Claude/Codex logins or subscriptions, Cursor API keys, OpenCode provider keys, or explicit API-key mode (`claim-conductor-sf-auth-strategy`, `claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-claude`, `claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-codex`, `claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-cursor`).
- Provider support: Anthropic/Claude-compatible routes, OpenAI/Codex, Cursor API, and OpenCode providers including OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, and GLM (`claim-conductor-sf-provider-support`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: Conductor injects workspace/system and UI-action prompts (`claim-conductor-sf-context-behavior`). Durable guidance uses repository settings plus `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / skills (`claim-conductor-sf-context-instruction-files`).
- Memory: workspace `.context` notes and handoffs can live without being committed; a separate persistent-memory product is not established (`claim-conductor-sf-memory`).
- Compaction: unknown (`claim-conductor-sf-compaction`).
- Session behavior: archive/restore keeps chat history (`claim-conductor-sf-session-behavior`); each chat tab uses one harness and one model, and workspace chats share a branch (`claim-conductor-sf-session-per-tab`); cloud sleep/wake has a 4-hour idle sleep and 23h50m hard stop (`claim-conductor-sf-cloud-sleep`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: terminal, Run button, Spotlight testing, Diff Viewer, Checks, and pull requests (`claim-conductor-sf-tools`); setup and run scripts (`claim-conductor-sf-tools-setup-scripts`).
- Extensions: a Conductor-owned plugin marketplace is unknown (`claim-conductor-sf-extensions`).
- MCP: harness-native MCP for Claude Code and Codex; Cursor Composer MCP is configured in Cursor (`claim-conductor-sf-mcp`).
- Skills: documented for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode (`claim-conductor-sf-skills`).
- Hooks: unknown as a Conductor-owned system (`claim-conductor-sf-hooks`).
- APIs: beta HTTP API at `https://api.conductor.build/v0` for cloud workspaces (`claim-conductor-sf-api`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: workspace-per-shippable-unit, then review, PR, merge, and archive; GitHub/Linear issue-to-PR is documented (`claim-conductor-sf-orchestration`, `claim-conductor-sf-issue-to-pr`).
- Parallelism: multiple independent workspaces, or multiple agents in one shared workspace (`claim-conductor-sf-parallelism`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: Git worktrees locally, explicitly not a security boundary; Conductor Cloud uses isolated Linux sandboxes (`claim-conductor-sf-isolation-worktrees`, `claim-conductor-sf-isolation-not-security`, `claim-conductor-sf-isolation-cloud-sandbox`). Cloud FAQ names Vercel sandbox hardware and Amazon Linux 2023 (`claim-conductor-sf-isolation-cloud-specs`).
- Permissions: local agents inherit the Mac user account and are not sandboxed; some tool calls can ask for approval (`claim-conductor-sf-permissions-user-account`, `claim-conductor-sf-permissions-approvals`).
- Security: live privacy docs say local chats stay on the Mac and traffic goes to the model provider, and the same page now documents cloud server storage (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local-2026-08-15`). A 2026-08-14 observation recorded an absolute none-stored-on-Conductor-servers clause (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local`). Cloud FAQ says local Conductor does not access coding inputs or outputs (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local-no-access`); cloud docs say Conductor stores cloud session inputs and outputs (`claim-conductor-sf-security-cloud`). The legal Privacy Notice says optional title-generation may send the first local chat message to a third-party provider (`claim-conductor-sf-security-title-generation`).
- Data path: live privacy page names local Application Support, stored account data, and PostHog analytics, and does not name Fly Postgres (`claim-conductor-sf-data-path-local-2026-08-15`); a 2026-08-14 observation recorded Fly Postgres (`claim-conductor-sf-data-path-local`); cloud chats on Conductor servers (`claim-conductor-sf-data-path-cloud`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Keep native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell routes distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Desktop local: `surface-conductor-macos-local` (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-macos-local`). Install-page evidence does not establish `approve_actions` or `session_continuity`; those stay `unknown` on the surface row. Product-level tool approvals are `claim-conductor-sf-permissions-approvals`. Product-level archive/restore is `claim-conductor-sf-session-behavior`.
  - Remote client to vendor cloud: `surface-conductor-macos-cloud` (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-macos-cloud`, `claim-conductor-sf-remote-cloud`)
  - API: `surface-conductor-api` (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-api`)
  - Generic remote shell: `surface-conductor-cloud-ssh` (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-cloud-ssh`)
- Remote behavior: the API can start and resume vendor-cloud agents (`claim-conductor-sf-api`). The Mac-as-cloud-client surface evidence establishes continue-until-sleep, so Mac-cloud `remote_resume` stays unknown (`claim-conductor-sf-surface-macos-cloud`, `claim-conductor-sf-remote-cloud`). Local Mac sessions stop when the machine closes (`claim-conductor-sf-execution-local`). Native-mobile, first-party mobile-web, first-party messaging, private-network, and Termux routes were not established.
- Mobile behavior: the Pro feature list says the mobile app is coming very soon (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-coming-soon`); the same pricing page later lists “our mobile app” without that qualifier (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-pricing-faq-wording`); Cloud FAQ still says “our mobile app (coming soon)” (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-cloud-faq`); the 0.77.0 changelog describes mobile-app UI (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-changelog`). No `ios`/`android` surface row is staged.
- Background behavior: cloud agents continue after the app closes; local sessions stop; chats can show background-task wait state (`claim-conductor-sf-background-cloud`, `claim-conductor-sf-background-local-stops`, `claim-conductor-sf-background-tasks`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: public page lists Free $0, Pro $50/mo, Teams $60/mo/user, and custom Enterprise (`claim-conductor-sf-pricing-plans`). The docs FAQ still describes a free tool that does not currently make money (`claim-conductor-sf-pricing-faq-free`). Model usage is billed by the provider, not resold by Conductor (`claim-conductor-sf-pricing-no-model-resale`).
- License: proprietary commercial Customer Terms, not an open-source license for Conductor itself (`claim-conductor-sf-license`).
- Maintenance: active changelog through 0.81.0 on 2026-08-13 (`claim-conductor-sf-maintenance`, `claim-conductor-sf-version`).
- Lock-in: unknown as a dedicated field. Related facts are macOS-only local install, bundled harness binaries, and cloud data stored on Conductor servers (`claim-conductor-sf-drawback-macos-only`, `claim-conductor-sf-wraps-cli-claude-code`, `claim-conductor-sf-data-path-cloud`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: unknown. The harnesses overview describes a workspace layer around existing harnesses but does not state a fork or original-product lineage claim (`claim-conductor-sf-lineage`).
- Relationship edges:
  - `conductor --orchestrates--> claude-code` (`claim-conductor-sf-orchestrates-claude-code`)
  - `conductor --orchestrates--> codex-family` (`claim-conductor-sf-orchestrates-codex`)
  - `conductor --orchestrates--> cursor` (`claim-conductor-sf-orchestrates-cursor`)
  - `conductor --orchestrates--> opencode` (`claim-conductor-sf-orchestrates-opencode`)
  - `conductor --wraps_cli--> claude-code` (`claim-conductor-sf-wraps-cli-claude-code`)
  - `conductor --wraps_cli--> codex-family` (`claim-conductor-sf-wraps-cli-codex`)
  - `conductor --wraps_cli--> opencode` (`claim-conductor-sf-wraps-cli-opencode`)
  - `conductor --reuses_auth_from--> claude-code` (`claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-claude`)
  - `conductor --reuses_auth_from--> codex-family` (`claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-codex`)
  - `conductor --reuses_auth_from--> cursor` (`claim-conductor-sf-reuses-auth-cursor`)
  - Cursor is API-only; no `wraps_cli` edge to `cursor` (`claim-conductor-sf-cursor-not-wraps-cli`).

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
Use `comparison-neighborhoods.jsonl` memberships. None were written.

- Comparison neighborhood IDs: unknown
- Substitutes: unknown
- Partial substitutes: unknown
- Same-lineage relatives: unknown
- Often-confused products: unknown
- Complements: the four orchestrated harnesses are relationship targets, not neighborhood memberships (`claim-conductor-sf-compatibility`).

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: a workspace layer around Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode sessions in isolated workspaces (`claim-conductor-sf-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: macOS-only local app, unsandboxed local agents, and cloud sleep/lifetime limits plus server-side cloud chat storage (`claim-conductor-sf-drawback-macos-only`, `claim-conductor-sf-drawback-no-local-sandbox`, `claim-conductor-sf-drawback-cloud-lifetime`, `claim-conductor-sf-data-path-cloud`).
- Best fit: unknown. The docs introduction does not name a specific intended-user persona (`claim-conductor-sf-intended-user`).
- Not-for: Windows/Linux users today, and users who need local isolation as a security boundary (`claim-conductor-sf-not-for-windows-linux`, `claim-conductor-sf-not-for-security-boundary`).

### Unresolved contradictions

- Vendor string: Terms say Melty Labs, Inc. (`claim-conductor-sf-vendor-melty-labs`); Privacy Notice says Melty, Inc. (`claim-conductor-sf-vendor-melty-inc`).
- Harness list: homepage names Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor (`claim-conductor-sf-homepage-omits-opencode`); docs name those three plus OpenCode (`claim-conductor-sf-compatibility`).
- Pricing: public pricing lists paid Pro/Teams/Enterprise plans (`claim-conductor-sf-pricing-plans`); the docs FAQ still says Conductor does not make money and is a free tool (`claim-conductor-sf-pricing-faq-free`).
- Funding: the official blog reports a $22M Series A on 2026-03-30 (`claim-conductor-sf-funding`); the docs FAQ still says the company is running on seed funding (`claim-conductor-sf-funding-faq-seed`).
- Chat storage: live privacy docs say local chats stay on the Mac and cloud chats are stored on Conductor servers (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local-2026-08-15`, `claim-conductor-sf-data-path-cloud`, `claim-conductor-sf-security-cloud`). A 2026-08-14 observation recorded an absolute none-stored-on-servers clause (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local`).
- Local chat access: live product privacy says they do not access local chats (`claim-conductor-sf-security-local-2026-08-15`); the legal Privacy Notice says optional title-generation may send the first local chat message to a third-party provider (`claim-conductor-sf-security-title-generation`).
- Mobile: Pro feature list says coming very soon (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-coming-soon`); the same pricing page later lists “our mobile app” without that qualifier (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-pricing-faq-wording`); Cloud FAQ still says coming soon (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-cloud-faq`); 0.77.0 changelog describes mobile-app UI (`claim-conductor-sf-mobile-changelog`).
- Local vs cloud sandbox: local agents are explicitly unsandboxed (`claim-conductor-sf-permissions-user-account`); the Cloud overview says each cloud workspace is an isolated Linux sandbox (`claim-conductor-sf-isolation-cloud-sandbox`); Cloud FAQ names Vercel sandbox hardware and Amazon Linux 2023 (`claim-conductor-sf-isolation-cloud-specs`).

First-party Open via SSH action uses generic SSH/Remote SSH to reach the sandbox. Wakes a sleeping workspace. Not a first-party mobile UX.

Same Mac app attached to Conductor Cloud Vercel sandboxes. Pro/Teams/Enterprise. Cloud overview evidence establishes continue-until-sleep, not wake/resume. Wake after sleep is claim-conductor-sf-cloud-sleep on working-with-cloud-workspaces, so remote_resume stays unknown on this evidence row.

Local git-worktree workspaces run on the same Mac. Install-page evidence does not establish session continuity; product-level archive/restore is claim-conductor-sf-session-behavior on the workflow page. Tool inspection and tool-call approvals were not established on this evidence claim. Approvals are claim-conductor-sf-permissions-approvals.
